rv.q: It is funny, moving and messily human.

Deftly directed by Sally Reid, Inexperience is expertly performed drama themed around desire, denial and the pursuit of happiness – but it’s also aimless and overlong, and fails to fully capitalise on an original and playful premise.
Whatever it is, though, it has intellectual depth, a glorious sense of humour, and a wonderful erotic energy...

cn.t: Douglas Maxwell's sparky romantic comedy earns praise for its clever conceit about a couple who sustain their relationship without physical contact, with critics applauding the brilliant comic style and expert performances.
